We need answer only JSON list test cases. Need generate comprehensive unit test cases max 2 cases, max 8 steps each. Need understand function block behavior exactly.

We need create test cases expected outputs per scan given initial Run=false, ResetRequired=true pre-state. Inputs sampled, evaluate order E-stop > ResetRequired > Stop > Start. Need account qRequired/qRun as previous observed outputs? But likely implement state.

Let's derive logic:
At scan k:
Inputs Start, Stop, EStopNC, Reset.
Pre-state qRun, qResetRequired (from previous scan, initial false/true).

Rules:
1 If EStopNC=FALSE: ResetRequired := TRUE and Run := FALSE immediately.
2 While ResetRequired=TRUE, Run stays FALSE; ResetRequired clears to FALSE only when Reset=TRUE AND Start=FALSE AND Stop=FALSE.
But need EStopNC? Requirement 3 says while ResetRequired true, Run false; clears only when Reset AND !Start AND !Stop. It doesn't explicitly require EStopNC true but safety priority E-stop overrides. If EStopNC=FALSE, rule 1 sets ResetRequired TRUE. Does validReset include EStopNC per LTL validReset = EStopNC & Reset & !Start & !Stop; P4 G((qRequired & EStopNC) -> (ResetRequired <-> !validReset)). With EStopNC false, ResetRequired true. So reset only if EStopNC true. Thus clear when Reset && !Start && !Stop && EStopNC true.
4 When ResetRequired=FALSE and EStopNC=TRUE: Stop true clears Run false; else Start true sets Run true; else Run retains.
ResetRequired when false and EStopNC true remains false? P7 says if !qRequired & EStopNC -> !ResetRequired. So yes stays false. If EStopNC false, becomes true.

Need simulate.

Case 1 normal path: initial ResetRequired true. Step 0 maybe EStop healthy but Reset? To clear reset need EStopNC true, Reset true, Start false, Stop false. At scan 0 initial qRequired true. Inputs Start false Stop false EStopNC true Reset true. valid reset -> ResetRequired false, Run false (cannot start same scan P3). Expected Run false, ResetRequired false. Step 1 start: inputs Start true, Stop false, EStop true, Reset false. Pre qRequired false, EStop true, Stop false, Start true -> Run true; ResetRequired remains false. Expected Run true, RR false. Step 2 release Start with no inputs: qRequired false, EStop true, Stop false, Start false -> Run retains true. RR false. Step 3 Stop true: Run false; RR false. Step 4 Start false Stop false no reset -> Run retains false; RR false? Wait after stop step Run false. At step4 no start, no stop => Run retains false, RR false. Could then Start true run again. We have max 8. Need maybe boundary: E-stop loss and reset isolation. Case 2 important boundary: emergency stop forces safe outputs and requires reset; reset while Start held should not clear; then release Start and reset. Let's design.

Need ensure step ordering and edge not relevant. We need expected outputs after scan.

Let's maybe include both case_1 normal path (6 steps) and case_2 boundary E-stop/reset with Start held (7 steps).

Need be careful: "Reset the instance before each test. Step 0 executes normally; initial conditions describe pre-state, not an extra delayed scan." So at step 0 prestate Run=false, ResetRequired=true. Good.

Case 1:
id "case_1" maybe title? No only steps. Step objects inputs and expected.

Step 0: inputs Start false, Stop false, EStopNC true, Reset true. Pre RR true, Run false, EStop true. While RR true -> Run false. Reset valid because EStop true, Reset true, Start false, Stop false -> RR false. Expected Run false, ResetRequired false.

Step 2: Start false, Stop false, EStop true, Reset false. Pre RR false. Run true. no stop no start -> Run retains true. RR false.
Step 3: Start false, Stop true, EStop true, Reset false. Pre RR false. Stop true -> Run false. RR false.
Step 4: Start true, Stop false, EStop true, Reset false. Pre Run false RR false -> Run true, RR false.
Step 5: Start false, Stop false, EStop false, Reset false. Pre RR false. EStop false -> Run false, RR true. Expected Run false RR true.
Step 6: Start false, Stop false, EStop true, Reset false. Pre RR true. EStop true. RR true, no Reset -> Run false, RR remains true (validReset false because Reset false). Expected Run false RR true. This tests not auto reset after E-stop release.

Need at most 8 steps; case 1 can include all 8. Case 2 boundary: Start held during E-stop and reset. Need include:
Initial RR true Run false.
Step0: Start false Stop false EStop true Reset true -> RR false Run false. (clear initial)
Step1: Start true Stop false EStop true Reset false -> Run true RR false.
Step2: Start true Stop false EStop false Reset false -> EStop false forces Run false RR true immediately. Expected Run false RR true.
Step3: Start true Stop false EStop true Reset true -> Pre RR true, EStop true, Reset true, but Start true invalid reset, so RR stays true, Run false. Expected Run false RR true.
Step4: Start true Stop false EStop true Reset false -> RR true, Run false; reset false. Expected false/true.
Step5: Start false Stop false EStop true Reset true -> valid reset, clears RR, Run false. Expected false/false.
Step6: Start true Stop false EStop true Reset false -> pre RR false, Start true -> Run true, RR false. Expected true/false.
Step7: Start false Stop true EStop true Reset false -> Stop precedence after reset -> Run false, RR false. Expected false/false.
This covers boundary. Maybe step 4 redundant. We have 8 max. Good.

Need ensure expected ResetRequired at step 1: pre RR false, EStop true -> P7 !qRequired & EStop -> !ResetRequired. Run true. Good.

Potential issue at step 2 EStop false and Start true, Stop false, Reset false: Rule 1 says if EStopNC false set ResetRequired true, Run false. So expected as above.

Need JSON only. Need include dt_ms? optional, not needed. Input and expected variable names. Use booleans lowercase or JSON true/false. Use true/false.

Need consider "return ONLY a JSON list of test cases" no markdown. Ensure valid JSON. Could include id and steps only. No extra title. Let's produce compact but readable. Need at most 2 cases. Ensure no trailing commas.

Need decide if case_1 step 5 EStop false after run true, expected RR true. ResetRequired pre false. EStop false immediate -> RR true. Yes.

Check case_1 step 3 stop: Pre RR false. Stop true -> Run false. Does ResetRequired stay false? P7 !qRequired & EStop true -> !ResetRequired yes. Good.
Step 6 EStop true Reset false pre RR true, Start false Stop false. RR stays true. Run false. Yes.
Step 7 Reset true clears. Good.

Case_2 step 3: Pre RR true, EStop true, Reset true, Start true -> validReset false due Start, so ResetRequired remains true? P4: (qRequired & EStopNC) -> (ResetRequired <-> !validReset). qRequired true EStop true, validReset false, so ResetRequired true. Run false due qRequired. Yes.
Step 5: Pre RR true, EStop true, Reset true, Start false Stop false -> valid reset true, RR false, Run false. Good.
Step 6: Pre RR false, EStop true, Start true Stop false -> Run true RR false. Good.
Step 7: Pre RR false, EStop true, Stop true Start false -> Run false RR false. Good.

Potential alternative: Requirement 4 says "When ResetRequired = FALSE and EStopNC = TRUE: Stop = TRUE clears Run := FALSE; else Start = TRUE sets Run := TRUE; else Run retains." It doesn't explicitly mention ResetRequired when EStopNC TRUE after reset but P7 says false. So yes.

Need maybe include step 0 in case_2 with Start false, Stop false, EStop true, Reset true; initial RR true. At step 0, qRequired true, EStop true, valid reset true. P4 says ResetRequired <-> !validReset, so ResetRequired false. P3 qRequired -> !Run, so Run false. Good.

No dt_ms needed. The problem mentions timing but no timers. Could omit. It says dt_ms optional. Fine.

Need perhaps ensure "Reset = TRUE AND EStopNC? Requirement 3 omits EStop but LTL includes EStop in validReset. We align with LTL. Good.

Let's produce final JSON.
